job: Riverside House AOV Smoke Vents (RRR Group)
_note: 2no bottom-hung AOV smoke vents, one per stairwell, at each stairwell's top storey. Priced off A Plus QT51518 supply-only, made supply-and-fit. Requirement source: red note on drawings K1653-11 and K1653-12, 'AUTOMATICALLY OPENABLE VENT/WINDOW WITH A FREE AREA OF 1m2'. Adam ruled on REQ-9 27/07: the openings are being newly formed, so the vents can be made as large as the free area requires - size is not a constraint. CURRENCY CAVEAT: the requirement appears ONLY on K1653-11 and K1653-12, neither ever revised since Mar 24, while the ground floor plan K1653-10b was revised twice in Nov 25. Confirm both sheets are still current - brief C5.

spec_items.ref: AOV smoke vent to Stairwell 1 top storey
AOV smoke vent to Stairwell 2 top storey
External mastic to vent perimeters (10.64 lm)

AOV control panel, mains + battery supply, cabling, containment, fire brigade override at ground floor access level, commissioning, EN 12101 O&M. STILL EXCLUDED from our price, but 28/07 we are at last ASKING THE PARTY WHO HOLDS THE INFORMATION as well as the one who owns the decision. RRR are asked who is carrying it (Questions to RRR item 8); A Plus are now asked what panel they would recommend for 2no 24v actuators, whether they supply it or it is always a separate trade, and to price it if they can (RFQ item 10). A Plus supply the actuator and their own notes say it 'must be powered by a compatible control system which is approved by SE Controls', so they are best placed to answer - and they had been left out because we had decided the scope boundary. A scope boundary says what a supplier will SUPPLY, not what they can TELL you. Found by running Gordon Court's two-letters asymmetry check in the form that applies to a one-supplier job.

Window restrictors - RECLASSIFIED 28/07 and now a PROVISIONAL, not a bare exclusion. Applying Gordon Court's rate-versus-quantity lens: this is a QUANTITY KNOWN (2no), NO RATE ANYWHERE item - the register has no restrictor category - so the only way to put a number on it is a supplier figure, and A Plus can give one. It also should not have sat quietly excluded: A Plus's own AOV notes put the duty on 'the facade contractor / fabricator', and on this job FENSTER ARE THE INSTALLER, so that is us. They further disclaim liability for replacement actuators or damage to the vent if no restrictor is fitted 50mm beyond the stroke, on a life-safety system. Now Part One item 8 - price 2no so the cost of carrying them can be compared against the cost of excluding them.
Builder's work - forming/adapting/making good openings, lintels, internal finishes
Access equipment / scaffold to top-storey level
Ongoing maintenance of the life-safety system (RRO 2005 duty of occupier/agent)

Part K anti-fall protection / balustrading if vent cill below 1100mm FFL, and the BS EN 60335-2 trap hazard below 2.5m FFL. 28/07: this was EXCLUDED BY BOTH PARTIES AND ASKED OF NEITHER - A Plus expressly exclude the Part K protection and we exclude it too, on a life-safety system in a stairwell, and it had sat as RFI-5 since the first day without reaching either letter. Both depend on cill height, which only the architect can state. Now question 8 of the RRR letter. Found by running the decision-versus-information diff properly across 14 topics rather than from memory - 12 came back clean.
W1 escape windows and W2 windows throughout the flat conversion (drawings K1653-10b/11/12 key, U 1.6)
D1 flat entrance doors FD30s and D5 external quality glazed door (drawings key, U 1.6)

VENTILATOR-NOT-WINDOW TEST (Gordon Court, 27/07) - confirmed A Plus QT51518 prices the AOV FUNCTION, not a plain window: the quote carries 'AOV Type 850mm Stroke Single', 'AOV Cable Direction', 'AOV Colour 9006 Satin', a dedicated AOV Notes page and the SE Controls actuator warranty, at GBP 1,401.24/m2 against GBP 528.83/m2 for a plain glazed aluminium window in the same size band. Gordon Court's BSW quote failed this test - 3no WN_7 at GBP 412.67/m2 and 4no WL_1 at GBP 442.98/m2 with zero occurrences of AOV, actuator, chain, stroke or 24V.

Onward haulage from Fenster's MK13 9HF yard to site at HP19 7HL - RECLASSIFIED 28/07 from excluded to PROVISIONAL, second item of the same class as the restrictors. Gordon Court's sharper test - 'we exclude X' is only safe if X is genuinely somebody else's under the spec - fails here: Fenster are the installer, so getting material from our own yard to site is OURS. It was excluded because nobody had priced it, not because it belongs to another package. Quantity known (1 delivery), no rate anywhere, so a supplier figure is the route - already brief item 6(b), which asks A Plus to quote delivery direct to HP19 7HL as an alternative. QT51518 carries NO site address and is addressed to our own Bradwell Abbey yard; A Plus also require 'suitable labour at the delivery point to unload'. AND A TRAP TO AVOID WHEN THE PROPOSAL IS WRITTEN: Gordon Court's issued proposal excludes Site Storage on the basis that 'Materials will be delivered to site', which contradicts every supplier quote they hold. Riverside has no proposal yet - do not let that wording in, because A Plus deliver to Milton Keynes.

Structural alteration to form or ENLARGE a vent opening - lintels, cutting masonry, making good. CORRECTED 27/07 latest: NEITHER VENT HAS A COST-FREE RESIZE. AOV.01 (second floor) has no opening in any stairwell wall so a new one must be formed, but 'new' is not 'free' - what matters is what it is cut into, and Riverside is existing fabric throughout (K1653-04 is a SINGLE existing/proposed elevation set, no added storey shown, no new construction annotated, cornice and pediment continuous through all three storeys), so it is cut into RETAINED masonry. AOV.02 (first floor) has three existing openings, so if the vent takes one its size is set. The earlier note that AOV.01's size was 'genuinely free' is WITHDRAWN - it was this chat's own error, caught by Gordon Court correcting the same mistake on their job. Inference from the elevations, not proof; the existing and demolition plans settle it. Brief C2. CORROBORATED 27/07 latest by a second independent instrument: the plans colour-code every NEW or ALTERED wall (new partition, new separating wall upgrade, separating wall upgrade to existing, blockwork infill), and at BOTH stairwells the internal walls are coded while the external walls carry no coding at all - i.e. retained existing fabric. Gordon Court have since withdrawn the WINDOW TAG as a statement of opening condition (their WE_2 windows sit in new stud walls), but that does not touch this job: Riverside has no such tag and the reasoning never used one. REMAINING GAP: no external wall BUILD-UP legend, so we know these walls are not new but not what they are made of - which decides the lintel, the fixing and the cost of forming the opening. A wall type schedule or section is now requested with the demolition and existing plans at C2.

Planning risk on a resize - drawings stamped 24/02303/PAPCR, a PRIOR APPROVAL reference rather than a full permission. Prior-approval conversions normally limit external alteration, so enlarging the openings may need a separate application. HD Planning to confirm - brief C3.

WALL WINDOW OR ROOF VENT on AOV.01 - replaces our withdrawn arched-head flag (the two arched-head windows on Elevation F line up with the Living room's W2 pair, not the stairwell). The second floor stairwell has NO opening in any of its walls and the note says the stair is to be vented 'AT THE TOP STOREY ROOF'. A Plus have quoted a wall casement on a 155mm subcill. If a roof vent is intended, the quoted unit is the wrong product from the wrong supplier - brief C4. THIRD POINTER ADDED 27/07 latest: Gordon Court's NBS names the standard product for this exact duty as 'STAIRWELL VENTILATOR... ROOF MOUNTED ONTO HORIZONTAL KERB... 1m2 geometric free area' - same duty, same 1m2, roof mounted - with a DIFFERENT model specified where a wall unit is wanted. So three independent pointers now say AOV.01 may be a roof vent: the note's wording, the absent wall opening, and the standard product for the duty. If it is, none of Part One of the brief applies to AOV.01 and the priced unit is wrong - roughly half the quote.

PACK COMPLETENESS (Gordon Court's 25-of-82 check, run 27/07 late) - we hold Campbell Ark's K1653-03/04/10b/11/12 plus hd planning's location plan, with K1653-01, 02, 05, 06, 07, 08 and 09 unaccounted for. The plans cross-refer to DETAIL 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 and no detail sheet is held. No fire strategy, no existing plans, no demolition plan, no sections, no window schedule; CORRECTED 28/07 - the OneDrive job folder is NOT empty (that was our error, from searching a path that does not exist: the root is 'OneDrive - Fenster Glazing (1)'). It holds the full job structure, A Plus QT51518 filed 27/07 15:46, the MASTER COVER LETTER 31.05.2026.docx and MASTER PRICING DOC 10.07.2026.xlsx. What survives: the '3. Drawings' folder holds NO files, so none of the six drawings we work from is filed anywhere. Anything on those sheets is neither priced nor knowingly excluded - the exclusion below is stated on that basis. Fire strategy and demolition plan requested by name as brief C0 and C2; drawing register as C7. 28/07: the title block gives the handle - Campbell Ark job number K1653, drawn SC, 01234 709296, drawingoffice@aol.com. C7 now asks for the K1653 drawing register by number. AND C0 HAS BEEN REDIRECTED: there may be no fire strategy to request at all - no fire engineer is named on any of the six drawings and the smoke-vent note is Campbell Ark's own, in AD B language on a sheet keyed 'TO AD B1'. The question now goes to the author rather than to a consultant who may never have been appointed.

Untagged stair glazing - the stair windows are the only glazing on K1653-11/12 carrying no W1 or W2 tag, while every habitable-room window has one. They sit outside the tagged system, which is probably why the vents were never scheduled, and it bears on whether the drawings' 1.6 U-value binds them (RFI-6).

Cavity closers, cavity trays and jamb DPCs at the vent openings - CHECKED AND CORRECTLY NOT OURS (Gordon Court, 27/07). These accessories sit in NBS F30 'Accessories/sundry items for brick/block/stone walling', a MASONRY section, not L10 windows - so they are the bricklayer's even where a new opening is formed. Recorded as a knowing exclusion rather than a silent gap. Riverside's external walls are of unestablished construction (no build-up legend), so if they prove to be cavity these items will exist and belong to the builder's work package.

Intumescent perimeter seal - CHECK RUN, NOT APPLICABLE. NBS L10 cl.790 'Fire-resisting frames' requires the gap between frame and reveal to be filled with INTUMESCENT mastic or tape, and L10 is the windows section, so on fire-rated frames it is the glazing scope and ordinary mastic in a fixings line does not comply (Gordon Court, 27/07). Not applicable here: the AOVs are smoke vents in the EXTERNAL wall of a protected stairwell, so the perimeter seal is weathering, not compartmentation - fire separation on this building runs between the stair and the flats (FD30s doors, fire collars, separating wall upgrades), not through the external envelope. A Plus quote no fire rating and none is specified for these frames. Our priced external mastic at 10.64 lm x GBP 5 stands. Re-check if any vent is ever relocated into a compartment wall.

Structural design for a new opening in retained masonry - NO STRUCTURAL ENGINEER IS NAMED anywhere on the six drawings we hold. The notes name a heating engineer and an electrician and otherwise defer to site: 'CONTRACTOR TO ESTABLISH EXACT DRAINAGE LAYOUT', 'TO BE SITE AGREED WITH HEATING ENGINEER/ELECTRICIAN & TO SUIT BUILDING INSPECTOR APPROVAL', 'ELECTRICAL LAYOUTS ARE TO BE SITE AGREED WITH CLIENT'. So the opening Adam authorised enlarging may have neither a structural design nor a price behind it. Engineer's investigation drawings (brick/mortar sampling, GPR) requested at C2 - on a refurbishment that is where the wall build-up normally lives, and it is a different request from asking the architect. CLASSIFIED 28/07 (Gordon Court's admin-versus-design test): of Riverside's five deferrals only the DETAIL sheets are ADMINISTRATIVE - they are Campbell Ark's own K1653 series and can be asked for by number. Drainage defers to a contractor not yet appointed, boiler/heater to an unnamed heating engineer, electrical to the client, and the wall build-up to a structural engineer who is not named anywhere. Those are DESIGN gaps: there is no document to chase.

PART B COMPLIANCE IS NOT BACK TO BACK - a plus put it on us, our clause 16 disclaims it to the client. QT51518 Product Performance: "It is the responsibility of the Customer to ensure all building regulations (i.e. Part 'B', 'F', 'L', 'M' & 'N' and any others relevant to the building)... are adhered to. The Supplier does not warrant or represent that any Product supplied shall comply with any of the aforementioned standards unless where expressly stated to the contrary by the Supplier." Our clause 16 disclaims regulatory strategy and relies on the client's professional team. Part B is not an incidental attribute of an AOV smoke vent - it is the entire function of the product, so the one regulation it exists to satisfy is the one disclaimed upstream and accepted downstream. Bites directly on C0/C1: if the 1m2 is aerodynamic, 1.30m2 geometric gives ~0.78-0.81m2 and the shortfall is ours. Verified at source on page 3 of QT51518 and in templates/proposal-content.json clause 16.  ->  RAISED, and the remedy is pre-order and free. The clause reads 'unless where expressly stated to the contrary by the Supplier', so RFQ items 1 and 4 now ask A Plus to state the aerodynamic free area, the EN 12101-2 classification and the whole-window Uw ON the revised quotation rather than by reply - an express statement by the Supplier is what the clause turns on. Flagged to Adam in the covering note. Measurement and maintenance checked in the same pass and are consistent both ways - recorded as clean, not claimed as gaps.

QT51518 INCORPORATES A TERMS OF SALE WE HAVE NEVER HELD. The advisory notes say the 'A Plus Windows & Doors Limited Terms of Sale Revision V.01.2 - 08.01.2018' apply to the quotation and to any subsequent Contract, and that the definitions - including who the 'Customer' is in every responsibility clause - come from 'Revision V.01 - 03.11.2017'. Neither is attached. Checked the archive rather than assuming: six files in the whole Commercial archive have 'Terms of Sale' in the name (Bradford Watts, Elkins, HouseUP, Prince Build, Stepnell, Conamar) and all six are the same Quotation Advisory Notes_Jan2019 PDF, which is the summary and not the terms. Diffed that 2019 file against QT51518's advisory pages - 0.75 sentence similarity, the only substantive change in seven years being frames splitting at 5m rather than 4m.  ->  RAISED as RFQ item 11, asking for both documents. Also turned into a rule: check_incorporated_terms_held, registered as the seventeenth check, with 29 variants written before it shipped and persisted into --selftest. An incorporation by reference reads as though the terms are settled and hides that you cannot say what they are - unlike a quote with no terms at all, which is a gap you can see.

THE 1.30m2 GEOMETRIC IS A BARE-VENT FIGURE. QT51518 page 5: 'The output free area values do not allow for any obstructions, side walls, reveals or neighbouring vents.' Both vents sit in a reveal in existing masonry on a 155mm subcill. This is the first thing found that could erode the geometric margin itself - the 30% headroom over 1m2 has been treated as comfortable and it is headroom against an unobstructed number. Not quantified here and not guessed at.  ->  RAISED in RFQ item 1, asking whether the 1.30m2 changes once installed in a reveal and whether the figure quoted is the bare vent or the installed opening.

THE WIND LOADING CHECK AND THE FIXING CALCULATIONS HAVE NO OWNER. QT51518: mullion selection calculated to BS 6399 Part 2 'with a design windload of 1200Pa unless otherwise stated'; 'all design responsibility remains with the Customer and our calculations are not to be relied on for any design purposes whatsoever'; the Customer should carry out their own full wind loading check and 'undertake full structural calculations on all brackets/spigots supplied by A Plus'; fixing lugs, bolts and brackets are excluded. Our clause 16 limits us to measurement verification, supply and installation, and no structural engineer is named on any of the six drawings. So on a second floor elevation neither the check nor the fixing design is anybody's.  ->  RAISED both ways: RFQ item 12 asks A Plus to confirm 1200Pa is the figure used and what fixing components are included; RRR question 5 now asks who is carrying the wind loading check and the fixing calculation, or whether a structural engineer is to be appointed. Compounds the existing structural-design gap rather than being a new seat.

'Actuators to EN 12101-2 are not formally weather tested' (QT51518 page 5).  ->  CONSIDERED AND DECLINED, recorded so nobody re-derives it. These vents are the only opening in those stairwells and nothing in the pack sets a weather-tightness requirement against them, so there is no standard to test the statement against. Revisit only if a performance spec appears.

THE PRICE IS NOT DIVISIBLE BY TWO. QT51518: 'The Price is based on the materials quoted being ordered together, and in one phase. Orders for only part of the quote, or fabrication over multiple phases, may incur additional charges for paint surcharges, rolling set up charges, reduced material optimisation, delivery or increased fabrication costs. We strongly recommend that when placing all such orders, a re-price is requested.' Every description of this price so far has been 2 x a unit rate (2,422.61 + 412.50 = 2,835.11, x2, plus 160 install each) - correct as a build-up, wrong as a statement of what one vent costs. LIVE because of C2: if the second floor stairwell is vented at the roof rather than the wall, we order ONE unit from this quotation and A Plus expressly reserve the right to re-price the remainder. The exposure on C2 is therefore the lost unit PLUS an unquantified re-price on the one that stays.  ->  RAISED as RFQ item 13, asking what a single 1130 x 1530 vent to this specification would cost - before the architect answers C2 rather than after.

STORAGE HAS A THREE WORKING DAY CLOCK ON THE ONE JOB THAT IS WAITING ON SOMEBODY ELSE. QT51518: 'A Plus reserves the right to levy storage costs for all goods which remain uncollected 3 working days after first availability for collection/delivery', and 'Materials off Site: this quotation does not include for holding of materials off-site... In such cases upon receipt of a suitable letter of indemnity we would require payment for such materials.' Neither clause is unusual. What makes them live is the defining fact of this job: Adam is holding the submission until PHDB return building-works costs, the sequence is openings formed -> survey -> manufacture, and there is no programme date for forming the openings. A slip starts a storage clock three working days after manufacture and converts the balance into payment-before-delivery against a letter of indemnity. THE FIRST COST ON THIS JOB THAT GROWS WITH THE DELAY ADAM HAS DELIBERATELY ACCEPTED.  ->  RAISED as RFQ item 14 (how the three days run, and whether there is a normal holding arrangement) and as a second reason under RRR question 11 for giving a programme date. Not quantified - no rate stated on the quote and none invented.

Gordon Court's 'available on request' grep, run on QT51518 - CHECK RUN, CLEAN. Probed for 'available on request', 'on request', 'subject to our standard', 'conditions of sale', 'standard terms', 'as amended': all zero. 'Terms of Sale' returns four hits, all of them the named V.01.2 - 08.01.2018 / V.01 - 03.11.2017 already recorded. No further incorporation by reference on this quotation. One detail kept and not raised: the payment basis itself points into the unheld document - 'Deposit and cleared Funds Prior to delivery on first order (see... Terms of Sale Revision V.01.2 for more information)' - but A Plus are an established supplier here rather than a first order.  ->  REPORTED CLEAN. A check that only ever fires is not one anybody trusts.

Category-completeness sweep of 25 categories, built independently of both documents (scratchpad/riverside_category_sweep.py) after Gordon Court found their own ten-category list short by 'building regulations'. The fault here was different but the same family: last turn's sweep was DOCUMENT-driven, so it could only find categories A Plus chose to write about. Making good and testing/commissioning appear in neither document; testing and commissioning is already inside C6 and RFQ item 10(c) so it is not a new seat, and making good around a newly formed opening sits in the building-works package RRR question 5 already asks about.  ->  RECORDED, not raised as new items. The two that WERE new are the phased-order and storage findings above.

FENSTER'S OWN EXCLUSIONS SCHEDULE WAS NOT ON THE DOCUMENT WE WOULD ISSUE. The company has a standard INCLUSIONS/EXCLUSIONS table - twelve exclusions: site welfare, access/lifting equipment, site storage, fire stopping, waste removal, internal finishing, final clean, TESTING (on or off site), STRUCTURAL ALTERATIONS (to be completed by Main Contractor), DESIGN RESPONSIBILITY (design calculations, structural calculations and engineer approvals), traffic management, and 'dimensions provided by others are assumed to be accurate. Any additional costs arising from incorrect dimensions shall be treated as a variation'. It lives in templates/proposal-content.json, the proposal/cover-letter path. Riverside was generated from MASTER PRICING DOC.xlsx, WHICH HAS NO EXCLUSIONS SECTION AT ALL - verified cell by cell: 2 exclusion-ish cells in the Riverside file and 1 in the template, all of them VAT or spec notes. The only real exclusion on its face was H5's AOV control panel line, typed in by hand. AN EXCLUSION THAT IS NOT IN THE DOCUMENT YOU ISSUE IS NOT AN EXCLUSION.  ->  FIXED. A twelve-line exclusions block now sits at rows 33-45 of the pricing document. Totals verified untouched before and after the save: I23 is still =SUM(I9:I10)+I21 and the I21 array formula survived. New rule check_exclusions_reach_the_issued_document (18th) FAILS the job as it stood before the fix and passes after.

OUR OWN PRICING DOCUMENT INCORPORATED TERMS BY REFERENCE WITH NO NAME, REVISION OR DATE. Cell C31 read '** This pricing document should be read in conjunction with the Terms and Conditions.' That is exactly BSW's 'terms and conditions of sale, available on request' shape - which Gordon Court has spent two turns establishing is WORSE than A Plus's named incorporation, because a named one at least gives a request a subject line. We have been criticising it in two suppliers this week while doing it to our own client.  ->  FIXED. C31 now names the document, its issue date, and says a copy accompanies the quotation. Free before issue; a conversation after one.

WITHDRAWN: 'measurement is consistent both ways - we own it upstream and downstream.' Posted to the noticeboard, written into HANDOVER.md and into AI.md. Fenster's exclusions schedule says 'dimensions provided by others are assumed to be accurate. Any additional costs arising from incorrect dimensions shall be treated as a variation and charged accordingly', so Fenster do NOT unconditionally own dimensions.  ->  ON RIVERSIDE THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES, for a narrower reason than the one given: the 1130 x 1530 came from our own enquiry, not from others, so it is ours here. The general claim was drawn from one clause I had read rather than the schedule I had not. Corrected on the board and in the handover.

WITHDRAWN: 'testing and commissioning is already inside C6 and RFQ item 10(c), so it is not a new seat' - written last turn and wrong. Fenster expressly exclude 'Testing - on or off site testing'. A Plus test the actuator on local batteries only. So the witnessed test and certification of a completed LIFE-SAFETY SMOKE VENTILATION SYSTEM is excluded by us, excluded by our supplier, and was asked of nobody - the two-signature hole in its purest form, on the same job where that phrase was coined, and it was looked at directly and called covered.  ->  RAISED. RRR question 10 now asks separately who carries the witnessed test and the certificate building control will want, and who is arranging the RRO 2005 maintenance the occupier owes from handover. Also now an express exclusion on the pricing document.

NARROWED: 'the wind loading check and the fixing calculations have no owner.' Fenster's standard schedule DOES exclude them - 'design calculations, structural calculations and engineer approvals unless specifically included within our scope'. So the company has an answer and this job did not carry it, because the schedule was not on the document. Both halves matter: the general position was never unallocated, the specific job was.  ->  RECORDED. Now an express exclusion on the pricing document; RRR question 5 already asks who is appointed.

CATEGORY RE-PROBE WITH CONCEPT-DERIVED WORDING - Gordon Court's extension, that a first-principles category list probed with one supplier's phrasing is still that supplier's sample. Their re-probe found 8 false negatives of 10 on AFS. Run here (scratchpad/riverside_category_sweep_v2.py): FIVE false negatives. structural design of openings - A Plus do address it, the word was 'structural' not 'masonry'. windload, unloading labour, and part-order/size - all three found in FENSTER's own exclusions schedule, which v1 never reached. testing and commissioning - both parties exclude it, which is the withdrawal above. Gordon Court's widening of the part-order rule to cover SIZE as well as quantity is live here in both limbs: the aerodynamic answer could change the size (RFQ item 2) and the wall-or-roof answer could change the quantity (RFQ item 13). A Plus's Changes clause covers both - 'any variation in Specification, quality, quantity, Products, timescale, or method'.  ->  RECORDED; the findings it produced are the items above.

supplier_quotes.note: Frames 4662.15 + glass 171.31 + energy surcharge 11.76 = 4845.22, ties exactly to the stated Total - no extras block on this quote (the Gordon Court element-lines-vs-total test passes). Supply only, delivered, glazed. 'The Price stated in the quotation is open for acceptance for a period of 30 days'. Order value is 154.78 BELOW A Plus's 5000 ex VAT free-delivery threshold, so delivery is chargeable at 1/mile each way from Watford unless batched - see check_free_delivery_threshold.

performance.required: Free area 1.0 m2 per stairwell (drawings K1653-11 and K1653-12), basis geometric or aerodynamic NOT stated on the drawing
performance.evidence: A Plus state GEOMETRIC 1.30 m2 per vent on QT51518 and give no aerodynamic figure. On their QT51516 (Towcester Vale, same DualFrame 75Si AOV) aerodynamic runs 60-62% of geometric (0.49/0.81 and 0.54/0.87). On that ratio 1.30 geometric is ~0.78-0.81 aerodynamic, ~20% short of 1.0. Complies on geometric, fails on aerodynamic. A Plus have not been asked for the aerodynamic figure for these sizes - RFI-1. EVIDENCE ADDED 27/07 EVENING, POINTING TO GEOMETRIC: (a) the drawings name their own compliance route - the key on K1653-10b/11/12 reads 'MAINS OPERATED INTERLINKED HEAT DETECTOR TO AD B1', i.e. the prescriptive Approved Document B route, which expresses common-stair smoke vents as a free area; aerodynamic free area is the language of the engineered BS 9991 / EN 12101-2 route, which this pack is not on. (b) Gordon Court's NBS 9001 L20 cl.630 specifies the standard product for this exact duty as 'AXS140 STAIRWELL VENTILATOR - throat 1250mm x 1000mm - 1m2 GEOMETRIC free area', and 'aerodynamic' appears nowhere in that job's 186-page NBS, 140-page mechanical or 127-page electrical spec. Recommendation is geometric, so the vents as quoted comply by 30% - but capable stays unconfirmed because only the fire engineer or building control can rule on the basis. Requote brief written and ready to settle it either way: outputs/Riverside House - A Plus requote brief (for Gintare).txt. CONFIGURATION RESOLVED 27/07 LATE: the quoted 1.30 m2 reconciles exactly with the full inner frame aperture, 957 x 1357 = 1.2986 m2 (1357 = 1530 less two 86.5mm sections, 86.5 from the 957 daylight width). So the geometric free area quoted IS the clear opening of the whole frame, which means the entire frame opens as one bottom-hung leaf with the 176mm transom acting as a glazing bar within the sash - consistent with a single 850mm chain on a frame whose individual apertures are only 590mm high. Also passes Gordon Court's ratio flag: required 1.0 / 1.729 gross = 57.8%. RATIO CAVEAT 27/07 LATE: Gordon Court have WITHDRAWN the 'above ~60% of gross frame' rule of thumb after recomputing their own unit on the aperture (WN_7 went from 'cannot reach 1.5 m2' to 99.3% of it). Use the aperture, not the gross frame - but note an aperture is normally INFERRED from a nominal section depth, including ours (86.5mm from (1130-957)/2), so it is an estimate and not a compliance test. The clear opening is A Plus's figure to state. APERTURE SENSITIVITY, 27/07 late: Gordon Court quantified the caveat - on their unit a +/-5mm change in an assumed nominal section swings the answer across the compliance line (65mm 101.1%, 70mm 99.3%), so no aperture percentage is a compliance test. Accepted. The direction of inference differs here though: they PREDICT an unstated clear opening from an assumed section; we RECONCILE a figure A Plus published. Across head+cill from 150mm to 200mm our reconciliation moves only 101.6% to 97.9% of the stated 1.30 m2, and there is no line to cross - the test is whether it holds, not whether it passes. The configuration conclusion is robust; it stays an inference until A Plus confirm it (brief item 5).

performance.required: U-value 1.6 W/m2K, per the key on drawings K1653-10b/11/12 (W1, W2 and D1 all carry 1.6)
performance.evidence: QT51518 states a CENTRE-PANE glass figure only - '4-20-4 Clr Tough S Coat 1.2' - and no whole-window Uw. A Plus's own advisory notes set their default the other way: 'Unless otherwise stated, windows and doors will have a U-Value no better than 1.8.' Whether the 1.6 key value binds the stair AOV (which is called out only by the red smoke-vent note, not lettered W1/W2) is itself unconfirmed. Nobody has asked A Plus for a Uw - RFI-6. 28/07 - AND THE DECISION OWNER HAD NEVER BEEN ASKED. We asked A Plus for the figure (RFQ item 4) but nobody was ever asked whether 1.6 BINDS these vents at all. The stair vents are the only glazing on K1653-10b/11/12 carrying no W tag, which is exactly why it is ambiguous. Now question 7 of the RRR letter.
